utterances.text: It says: "Any weapon -- that all citizens who possess any kind of weapon shall hand it to the public security station. The closest unit of the Yugoslav People's Army or the staff of the Territorial Defence."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, but then it goes on to exempt those for which person has a licence or if they're members of Territorial Defence or police or JNA, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, I have no intention of twisting my neck. Put it straight. It was horizontal. That's perfect. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think I asked the question, but it -- the question was: "It exempts people who have licences, members of Territorial Defence formations, active and reserve police, and JNA? So it's dealing with illegally held weapons; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, it's not the document that I think he's being questioned on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No. It's not the document, 626 is the one he's being asked about, of 28 April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But don't you have the English version --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see, I see. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has answered the question yes, so I think we can move forward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if there was no Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region until 5 May of 1992, this conclusion about the surrendering of illegally held weapons couldn't have been as a result of any action of the ARK Crisis Staff, could it?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff took such a decision and published it, but of the radio they broadcast an announcement saying that all legally possessed and illegally possessed weapons should be surrendered. I know this very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've misunderstood my question, sir, and I'm sorry. It's probably my fault?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It is actually a comment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've misunderstood my comment, sir. My comment --

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If there was no ARK Crisis Staff on 28 April -- was it 28 April -- when this document was generated, it couldn't have resulted from an order of the ARK Crisis Staff, could it? It probably doesn't even need to be asked. I'll just withdraw it. Look at P164, please.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at P164 now, will you please. It should be right there. Have you found it? You talked the other day about paragraph 1 of that document --

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The other day you talked about paragraph 1 of that document and explained that that paragraph dealt with the appointment -- the replacement of personnel in the court system; in other words, the dismissal of Muslim personnel and their replacement by Serbian personnel. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that one is dated 29 April 1992, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next one that I want you to look at is 635. And I want to refer you to paragraph 7, which reads: "At the request of the Regional Crisis Staff, the Crisis Staff of the Sanski Most Serbian municipality appointed Vlado Vrkes deputy president of the Crisis Staff of the Sanski Most Serbian municipality." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find this document?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with it did you see a document from the Regional Crisis Staff that this document refers to saying, "please appoint Vlado Vrkes deputy president of the Sanski Most Crisis Staff"?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no, I didn't see such a document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I can deal with it in re-examination, but it seems to me sensible if Mr. Ackerman wants to pursue this if Your Honours take P227 and look at the decision of the 18th of May of the ARK Crisis Staff. It's in the gazettes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document I want to refer you to, sir, is P218.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It should be in the same binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] You're coming up with --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're coming up with a lot of documents you did not indicate to us. And we have a list from you which dates from yesterday with one, two, three, plus, plus, plus -- and then documents from OTP Sanski Most binders which leaves us guessing, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, that's almost exactly what the Prosecution told you, that they'd be referring to documents from those two binders. They didn't give you all the numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: They gave you all the numbers basically.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No, they didn't. They said we'll be referring to documents from these two binders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: They did say that as well. But the thing is that some of these documents obviously we don't have available right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I told you, Your Honour, I'd be referring to documents from the two Sanski Most binders.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And that's what I'm doing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In the binder, where is 218? What divider.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I don't have dividers. You invented those dividers. You didn't tell me where your dividers were. It comes after 648.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We've solved that. It's on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you have -- do you have 218, a Crisis Staff conclusion of 30 May 1992?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is a circled "2" in a paragraph that begins "A long-term solution." Can you find that?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the area, not the region. That's an area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have no idea what you're talking about. I'm trying to direct your attention to a circled number "2," which you will find on the second page of the document, second paragraph. Do you find that?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And first -- okay. The last sentence of that paragraph says: "Also make contact with the leadership of the Autonomous Region of Krajina regarding implementation of the idea on resettlement of the population." You don't know whether that contact was ever made, do you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the population from Mahala was expelled. They were forcibly expelled. And about the connection between the Crisis Staff -- or the municipality of Sanski Most and the Autonomous Region of Krajina, I didn't have the opportunity to --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. So the answer is you don't know?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To find out about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So answer is you don't know; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the officials, Rasula, Vrkes, those people in Sanski Most were not happy with the functioning of the ARK Crisis Staff and its leadership? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you look at P690, please. And that should be in volume 2, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I should point out I did -- we did look at this when I went through it with him in chief, this particular document. We read that particular paragraph. So I'm not sure there's a necessity for the judge to read that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see what the question is going to be, if there is a question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like you to look at paragraph 2(D). 2(D) says that "Every municipality on the territory of the Autonomous Region of Krajina shall appoint one representative for issues connected to removal and exchange of population and prisoners and report something by fax to Vojo Kupresanin"; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute you said 2(D). And it says something else here. I don't know if it has been correctly translated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't either. It's paragraph 2. And then under that, paragraph -- yeah, it hasn't been. Looks like the paragraphs go A, B, V, G.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's G, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yeah. It's G in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's G --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: In the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the B/C/S version, the paragraph that starts with [B/C/S spoken].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It says that, "Every municipality on the territory of the Autonomous Region of Krajina shall appoint one representative."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it appears that Vojo Kupresanin was designated as the person to coordinate this business of exchange of population; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that here, because it says, "Sent to Vojo Kupresanin by telefax." I don't know whether he was the person responsible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If you look on page 2 -- I don't know if -- the English version is paragraph I, but I don't think it's paragraph I in the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't have a paragraph I on page 2, Mr. Ackerman. Page 2, number 5 ends with paragraph F, the English version. It's paragraph 2 -- oh, I see what you mean. I see what you mean. Judge, turn over the page, the second page of that document, the very first paragraph at the top with the letter F -- or what looks like a letter F, [B/C/S spoken]. That's the one, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's it?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says. "The Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina are criticised for reaching decisions at the level of Banja Luka municipality that were important for the entire territory of the Autonomous Region of Krajina"; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I had asked you a moment ago, you'll recall, if you knew that the officials in Sanski Most were not happy with the ARK Crisis Staff and its leadership, and that was one of the paragraphs I wanted to point you to in that regard. I'd like you also to look at -- and let me ask you first: Do you know anything about an inter-municipal agreement of the Sanko Unska [phoen] area of 14 June 1992?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like you to take a look, please, at P247.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Which document?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's not in the binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It wouldn't be in the binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's on the list though -- or it better be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have P247, sir?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the Prosecutor's number, 392.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No -- well, maybe. Yes, that's the right one. This appears to have been a meeting held at Korcanica on 14 June 1992, with representatives from Srpska Krupa, Bosanski Petrovac, Bosanski Novi, Bosanska Dubica, Prijedor, and Sanski Most. If you look under a number -- I don't know if it has this number even. No, it doesn't. If you look on page 2, number 3(A) --

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't got page 2. There is no page 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's real helpful. I will give you my copy of this document. Now, you'll find a page 2 and you'll find a paragraph 3, "Joint positions." And under that, A: "We think that the work" --

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "We think that the work of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina under wartime circumstances should be much more serious and that its politicians and experts should pay more attention to the problems in all constituent municipalities of the Autonomous Region of Krajina." And then if you look at B: "Accordingly, we propose that Vojo Kupresanin be appointed president of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina." And then it goes on and says why. And if you look at paragraph E, then, just a little further down: "We think that the work of the Crisis Staff has been unsatisfactory and that it has been serving the local interests of Banja Luka." And then the next page, paragraph F, the second paragraph under F: "Accordingly, personnel changes should be made in the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina and with a view to urgently breaking with individuals who have decided to obstruct the work of the Serbian Democratic Party in the Autonomous Region of Krajina and to question the lofty goals which have galvanised the Serbian people." Now, that you have seen the document and become aware of its contents, do you have any memory of learning anything about this sort of break-away group that was trying to get Mr. Brdjanin replaced with Mr. Kupresanin?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I was in the Manjaca camp and we didn't have any information. We were totally isolated. We didn't receive any information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was really referring more to the investigation work that you've done after you've gone back, if you became aware of it in the course of those investigations. I know where you were at the time.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, the next document I want you to look at is P709. We're back in binder 2. And this, sir, is a document again from Sanski Most, the executive committee of the municipal assembly, signed Mladen Lukic, 30 July 1992. Paragraph 6: "That the government of the Autonomous Region of Krajina be urgently requested to approve the establishment of prisons." In your investigations did you find --

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your investigations, did you find any document from the Autonomous Region of Krajina approving the establishment of prisons?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember all the documents now because there was correspondence between the chief of the CSB, Zupljanin, and the chief of the public security station in Sanski Most, Vrucinic Mirko. But I can't remember this exactly now -- I can't remember all the documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't recall seeing a document along the lines of what this document says, a document approving the establishment of prisons, do you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you don't know whether this request was even ever forwarded to the government of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, do you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I don't know, since a copy was made -- since there was correspondence. But I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know if the interpretation has been right. Could you repeat slowly what you have said, because the way it's been interpreted to me doesn't really make much sense. You said "I am not sure --" can you carry on from there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure whether there was correspondence between the executive community of -- the executive committee and the Autonomous Region of Krajina, because I haven't seen these documents for a long time and they were -- well, that's why I say I'm not sure. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. We're going to go back into binder 1 again now and talk about a different subject. You recall that earlier today we revisited some of your testimony about the policeman coming to the jail in Sanski Most, and telling you that there were still 400 Green Berets in Mahala that hadn't given up yet and so the battle was still going on. You recall that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want you to look now at P638. You've seen it before. This is a document from the Territorial Defence, Nedeljko Anicic, regarding this armament operations in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And in the first paragraph, it speaks of the Green Berets, which were inserted into the Sanski Most area, the hostile villages and towns in Sanski Most. They've formed eight detachments, five independent companies, and a number of independent platoons in Mahala. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What it says here is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what it says. I'm just asking you if that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look over to paragraph 6 -- well, just above paragraph 5, it says that an attack will begin at 0500 on 26 May, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then I believe paragraph 6 deals with the Mahala area -- or does it?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mahala isn't mentioned here. These are other parts of the town, other neighbourhoods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's in paragraph 9 where they talk about neutralising the remaining fire targets and searching the Mahala sector. I just had the wrong paragraph. That's what it says; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at -- now at document P642. This again is a document you have seen before. It's dated 27 May 1992 from the 1st Krajina Corps command. It's a regular combat report. Right before numbered paragraph 2, it says: "The situation in Sanski Most is becoming increasingly complicated. At about 1500 hours in the area of Sanski Most, the Green Berets attacked a convoy of buses transporting conscripts, killing two conscripts and lightly or seriously wounding roughly 20 others. The command of the 30th Partisan Division was ordered to send in a combat group to rescue the convoy." And you haven't found this yet, have you? 642.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. The first page is missing here, in B/C/S, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, here it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] It's a three-page document, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He's got the first page now. And that's the only part I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the page number is 00861461.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have it. I have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to that part that talks about an attack by the Green Berets on a convoy of buses transporting conscripts. And you saw that the other day.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I think you told us the other day that you might have heard about that incident. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Sanski Most, no, I haven't heard about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If I can have my copy back and we can look now at P680?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: This is from the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We haven't got it. This is volume 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, you saw this document too the other day. It talks about a battle that went on at Vrhpolje, where it says there was a force of 800 men which you said you thought was about 300. What I'd like you to do is look at the next page. And that next page shows weapons that were confiscated, were handed over. And I just want to bring your attention to the fact that there seems to have been 30 submachine-guns, 227 automatic rifles, 155 semi-automatic rifles, 11 light machine-guns, 1 MTV - I don't know what that is. Do you know what an MTV is?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Four hand grenades, 5 zoljas, which are described as hand-held rocket launchers, 83 kilos of explosives, 218 pistols, eight sniper rifles, and 40 M-48 rifles. That's what that shows, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says in the document, but I don't know a thing about any of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at -- then at P699.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm now going to ask. Is there a question going to be put in any of this? Because so far not one question has actually been put about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But on the other hand, if he answers "I don't know anything about that," it is obvious that Mr. Ackerman can't then put a question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: There hasn't been a question so far. He hasn't been asked whether he know -- it's just been -- we've just been going through it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. But it is obvious that he's asking the witness whether he knows anything about it to start with.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then it's -- so it's up to him, because if the answer is yes, the reaction may be one way. If the answer is no, it could be another. I mean, many first questions that are -- than not followed by other questions. Go ahead, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Document P699 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All I know is that I have done my exercise for the day picking up these binders up and down. 699.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It might have been helpful for me just to put them all in one binder for Your Honours. Maybe I'll do that next time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at -- this is from the Sanski Most public security station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 699. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And right on the first page, it talks about some weapons that were -- it's dated 10 July. It talks about weapons that were returned. And it's a fairly long list of weapons, including explosives, ammunition, semi-automatic rifles, automatic rifles, carbines, light rifles; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here, but generally speaking -- I would like to add something -- that I think that this information is absolutely not correct. That's what I think in terms of the previous document too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, and there's a reason that you think that, which we'll talk about here in a moment, sir. And all I'm asking you now if you look now at the last page of that document, there is a list of the total number of weapons that were gathered in one way or another. It says "Total"; correct? And it says, 3.140 kilos of explosives, 5.000 rounds of ammunition, 278 automatic rifles, 161 semi-automatic rifles, 385 pistols. That's part of the list; right?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says in the list, but this is certainly not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know that's your position, sir. You've made it clear many times. Now, I'm going to a different subject now. I want you to again be provided with some documents that you saw the other day. And we'll start with DB74.1. And look at the very last page, sir. We looked at this document very briefly when we were talking about Zijad Ibric yesterday, and we see his signature there. And he signed that, I take it, because he was the interviewer and the person who took the statement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked to this person, and I took this person to the scene. I took him so that he would show me the place where he had to jump off the bridge in Vrhpolje as ordered by the Serb army and where he was shot at and where he hid in the water by the branches. There are also photo documents to prove that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: Why did Zijad Ibric sign this document?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because at that time I did not have a typist at court. That was the problem. So then I asked him to do the writing, being a professional in this regard. So he is just a technical person. He used a laptop to write all this. I know this person, this witness very well. He was in camp with me. And after the camp, he went to Germany and -- oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] It's such a simple question.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, Your Honour. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does it say above the signature of Zijad Ibric? Could you just read that, please.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Official of AID."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it doesn't say "typist" or "transcriber" but "AID official," doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirm this to you, that at that time he was a technical person. He was employed as a staff member in AID in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just asked you what it said. I said it doesn't say "typist" or "transcriber," does it? You can just say "yes" or "no," can't you? I mean, I'm trying to finish today. It was a simple question.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's an official of AID.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The witness, of course, signed it because he was the witness. That's fairly clear, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That witness is going to come here too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We know that. Why did you sign it?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah. What does it signify when you sign this document? What does that mean? What does your signature mean on this document?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means that I was carrying out an investigation. I interviewed this witness. This entire case related to the killing in his town, and there are other documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not part of the question I asked you. I only want to know what your signature means on this document. Does it certify that you were involved in this interview and that contents of that statement are true and correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now look at DB76.1. And again, sir, I just want to direct you to the last page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, sorry to butt in again, but I think yesterday we came to an agreement that 76.1 and 74.1 are a replica of one another, the same document. And in fact, I noted to you that in the first one 74.1 there was JMB 2309967 which was redacted in 76.1 B, but otherwise they are exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We can skip that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What's confusing me is the -- the lack of an ERN number at the top of one of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's skip that one, sir, and go to 75.1. Now, 75.1, sir, is another witness statement, I believe. And again, you told us that it bears your signature. And my only question is: Is that the same certification, that you're certifying that you were involved in the taking of this statement and that its contents are correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who is Halima Alagic?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Halima Alagic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is that?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She's a person who worked for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can we look now at 73.1. And again, the last page, sir. Just confirm for me that Mr. Ibric, Mr. Begic, and you signed it and that your signature is there to certify that you participated in the taking of the statement and that it's true and correct.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'd like the registrar to give to the usher 73.2, 74.2, and 75.2. And I'd like them arranged on the ELMO so that we can all see them. That's fine. Now, sir, there are three different signatures there, all of which you have told us are yours. Which of those is not yours?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All three are my signatures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at that one on the bottom, sir. You don't make an "L" like that "L" at the end of Adil. And you don't make a "C" like the "C" at the end of Draganovic. That is clearly written by someone else, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. If I say that it's my signature, then it's my signature. For me, it's the same signature. It depends on how I feel, and it depends on whether I'm in a hurry. I do my L's this way or that way, but it's my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you want to swear here under oath that all three of those signatures were made by you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I state that under oath.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know they can be examined by a handwriting expert?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why, yes. I don't mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think I can finish in 15 minutes, and I would like to -- I'd like to do this last segment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In fact, we have been sitting for an hour and a half, so it's time to break in any case. We'll break for 20 minutes, if that is okay with everyone. Madam Fauveau? I can't see you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll resume in exactly 30 minutes from now, and that's at 12.46.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. Your Honour said 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry, 20 minutes. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Twenty-five to or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Twenty-five to, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would ask the usher to hand the witness a blank piece of paper and a pen that I gave him a little while ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, please make the three signatures that you saw on the ELMO that you said were your signatures. Just make each one of them for me, please, in the order that you saw them on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've got several here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you've made -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Could the usher collect those, please. Let me see them for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think we should put them on the ELMO first for everyone to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before we give that document a proper formality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Could we have that marked as Defendant Brdjanin Exhibit 83, I believe it is. And then what I would like to do, Your Honour, is substitute a copy for the record, because I may want to use the original signatures for comparison purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're going to give it which number?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: DB83.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 83. And if you need to use it -- make use of it, Mr. Ackerman, you know what the procedure is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At -- on May 15th, sir, at page 5654 of the transcript, you were being asked by Ms. Korner about the municipal control -- municipal assembly control over the judiciary. And you gave the following answer: "I think they could not have issued any such orders to me and to other judges; neither could they do so to other judges." And then you said this: "But at that time the situation was different because I no longer had any control over the Serbian judges." Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the implication was that before that, you had had some control over the Serbian judges. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. It wasn't a matter of control in the normal sense of the term.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you never had any control over the Serbian judges, did you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance with the law and my authority as president of the court was quite clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So why did you tell the Chamber that you no longer had control, leaving the impression that you might have previously had control?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't mean control in the usual sense of the term. But judges of Serbian nationality no longer contacted me. They would no longer come to my office. They would go upstairs. And they -- they remained apart. Every day we couldn't see each other as colleagues in the court any more, as was common practice. That was normal. That's what I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about in your court today? Do you exert any control or influence over any of the lower court judges over whom you are the president?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's called the municipal court. I don't have any control, apart from the control that I have -- that is provided for in the law. So that authorises me to organise the administration and ensure that there are conditions for work in the court. I schedule the work. I assign cases, and the judges work on an independent basis, just as I am independent as a judge. That's quite clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a judge in your court by the name of Edina Redzisic?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a judge called Edina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Last name Redzisic?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Redzisic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Draganovic, I've alluded to this before today -- you have a very personal interest in convincing this Trial Chamber of many of the things that you have said to them during your testimony here today, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not in my interest to convince the Trial Chamber of anything, apart from convincing them of the truth. All I have been saying is the truth and nothing but the truth, and everything that I have been asked, everything that the Prosecutor has asked me and that you have asked me and the Trial Chamber too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It could help you personally, couldn't it, sir, if this Chamber were to find that you were telling the truth when you said there was no fighting in the Mahala neighbourhood in Sanski Most, couldn't it?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand by my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't answer my question. It could help you personally if this Chamber were to find that you're telling the truth when you say there's no fighting in the Mahala neighbourhood of Sanski Most. Is that a true statement or not? You can just say "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we'll get there.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 5480 of the transcript of 13 May 2002, you said: "The Serbian authorities removed me from the court illegally. Then they unlawfully arrested me and tortured me in the camp. And they also destroyed my property." What property? What property?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was thinking about my private property.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Consisting of what?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It consisted of a house, furniture, car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it destroyed?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was destroyed on the 27th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was it destroyed?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How was it destroyed?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. How?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't see it happen, did you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I only -- when we descended in the afternoon from the prison cells, I saw a lot of smoke in the air which was coming from the direction of Mahala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was very thick smoke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know who destroyed your house, do you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume -- I think I know who destroyed it, but there are some people who do know who did this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much compensation have you received through organisations of one form or another for the damage that was done to your home?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The amount was quite insignificant when compared to the damage that was done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't ask you if it was significant. I said how much did you receive?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some material and the worth of that material was under 10.000 -- under 10.000 convertible marks. Maybe 8.000 or even less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And since you believed that was not satisfactory compensation, you filed a lawsuit in an attempt to recover 100.000 Deutschmarks for damages to your property, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at DB69, please -- DB69 B. If you'd look at the very last page, sir. It is signed by you, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The date is 25 August 1997? It's there on the last page. Do you see it? Right by your signature.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in this lawsuit you accused seven people. And they're listed right there in the front, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You accused Nedjeljko Rasula and Bosko Banjac, and you say that they ordered and led destruction and burning of your dwelling house; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here. That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you wrote that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you said that the direct perpetrators of the destruction of your property, the total destruction of your property, were Dusan Mudrinic and Dusan Saovic who carried out the orders of Rasula and Banjac. That's what you're alleging; right?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're alleging they destroyed it by setting it on fire, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you say that you want to point out that the damage was caused away from any combat activities.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And it's important for you to establish that it was away from combat activities because otherwise you wouldn't be able to receive any compensation at all, would you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's important for me -- well --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't ask you what was important for you. Look at the question I asked you. It's important for you to establish that it was away from combat activities, because otherwise you wouldn't be able to receive any compensation at all, would you? Just answer that question.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That doesn't have to mean that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're familiar with the Dayton Accords regarding these matters, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with the Dayton Agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you have named Nedjeljko Rasula and Bosko Banjac as ordering the destruction of your house and Dusan Mudrinic and Dusan Saovic as actually doing it. But you also have brought action against Slobodanka Saovic, Jelena Indjic, Danica Cucum, and Dusanka Grbic. What did they do to your house?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't do anything to my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They just happened to be relatives of people who you think did something to your house, don't they?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were the legal inheritors of Saovic Dusan. They inherited his property, because he died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say he was died or did you say he was killed -- did you say he died or did you say he was killed?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dusan Saovic, as far as I know, he died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think he's saying killed and the translation is coming off as died. That's what I'm told?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The interpreters please. I am being told by Mr. Ackerman that the witness is using a word which ought to be translated or interpreted as "killed" while it is being translated twice already as "died." Which is the right interpretation? And I'm going to ask the witness to repeat what he said before. Judge, be patient. Did Dusan Saovic, or whatever his name is, die a natural death or was he killed? What did you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dusan Saovic was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So then what you asked for in addition to 100.000 Deutschmarks was that you asked the Court to impose temporary security measures to forbid the alienation of the real estate and burden of the real estate belonging to all these people who you had accused in this document, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you didn't detach to the document any documents from a court of probate showing that these people you sued were the legal heirs of the person who you claim is -- was killed, did you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. This is a formal complaint which was submitted. At the time -- I didn't have it at the time. But the court can obtain such documents in its official capacity. But other evidence was obtained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You filed this case in your own court, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The complaint -- yes, I filed it in my own court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... assignments, you assigned it to Edina Redzisic, a judge of that court, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to the schedule -- the annual schedule, the cases were submitted and cross-submitted to the Judge Edina Redzisic. But she's no longer in the court in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you got the Judge Edina Redzisic to grant your request and impose these temporary measures on all of this property, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Judge. I think I'm going to ask you to rephrase the question. Because and you got -- the judge seems to --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- To hint that he used undue pressure on Judge Edina.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I understood that was the suggestion Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. But this is why I'm asking him. If he's making that allegation, he needs to put it in no equivocal terms. I mean, it's -- because --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Judge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Having an interpretation between killed and died, I start doubting how it's being put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Judge, Edina Redzisic granted exactly what you had requested that she grant in terms of temporary measures, didn't she?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The judge adopted a temporary decision forbidding appropriation -- temporarily.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's exactly what you asked her to do, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the complaint, I also attached a proposal with the statement of reasons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at DB70 B, sir. The copy is not good, but I think you can read the second page, which is what I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: DB70 B.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the second page, the full paragraph starting at the top. "Since the complainant has presented the existence of the claim as probable and indicated the existing danger that the debtors, that is, accused, might obstruct or significantly complicate the payment of the claim by alienating their property, the Court has adopted the complainant's proposal and issued a decision as given above." And then it cites the articles of the law on executive procedures upon which it is based. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then the judge says: "It is not possible to file a special appeal against this decision"; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see what it says there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall if anywhere in this document where she refers to the complainant that she indicated that you were the president of the court? Do you recall that being in there?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. It's all very well to have a translation of something, but we don't know what it is that's written there, at that last line.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I understand it's very difficult to read.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to know how the translator managed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There probably was a better copy, and this probably got copied poorly, and I will try to find that better copy and substitute it, Your Honour, because Ms. Korner is right, there should be a better copy in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps, I mean, a very short question --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's not an important question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Then leave it. But you are definitely right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to look at DB68 B, sir. This document, sir, is a -- it's called an answer to the charge by the proxy of the fourth and seventh accused. And it's filed by a lawyer named Radovan Stanic from Prijedor. I assume you have seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I received this answer to the judge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you look about halfway through that first paragraph, right before the words -- the name Saovic Dusan, that lawyer says, does he not that, "The Court has without having a critical estimate regarding the proposed evidence and in contrary to the provisions in Article 265 and 266 ZIP, and without holding a preparatory hearing, issued a decision imposing temporary measures." That's what that lawyer argues in that answer; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to look at DB71 B. This, sir, is a document from the canton court in Bihac of 25 January 2001 regarding this same case.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the judge who signed this, the presiding judge, was Ilvana Pracic or something like that.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this court says: "The municipal court Sanski Most has filed with this court a request for delegation of another municipal court due to the fact that in the case P number 419/99, the complainant Draganovic, Adil has a legal post in the municipal court Sanski Most, and therefore -- at aiming at economic aspect, another court should be appointed." And the request was for the appointment of the municipal court in Kljuc; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who in the municipal court in Sanski Most filed the request for delegation of another municipal court because of your position? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the judge who was involved in this case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After she had entered the temporary orders that you requested; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The canton court in Bihac did not accept the recommendation to appoint the municipal court in Kljuc but instead sent the case to Bosanska Krupa; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to look at DB72 B, please. Now, this is a decision of the municipal court in Bosanska Krupa, and the judge is Asim Berberovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this decision was entered on 5 May 2001; yes?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so it had been almost 18 months since Judge Edina tied up the property of all these people before the court in Krupa entered its decision; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The judge did not tie up the property. It was just a ban on alienation that was registered in the land register.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. They couldn't sell it. They couldn't do anything with it. They couldn't sell it. They couldn't alienate. They couldn't do anything with it because of that order. That's what the order was all about; right?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not right. That's not right. They only couldn't sell it. That's what it meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that's what I said. They couldn't -- they couldn't mortgage it either. I mean, they couldn't borrow money on it and give a mortgage or -- I don't know what you call them in your country, but they couldn't do that either. They couldn't do anything to tie up that property and keep you from getting your hands on it if you won your case.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Look at -- look at this DB72 document, please. And under the word "decision," you'll see a paragraph beginning "Herewith is granted." And it says: "Herewith is granted the motion filed by the accused Banjac Bosko, Rasula Nedjeljko, Saovic, Bojanvokic [phoen], Slobodanka, and Grbic - born Saovic - Dusanka regarding the decision of the municipal court in Sanski Most number P419-99, dated 22 November 1999. And the temporary measure forbidding the alienation and burden of the real estate of the accused is in its whole revoked. The same applies for the actions carried out in the procedure." Now, apparently the persons accused by you filed a motion with the Court in Bosanska Krupa asking that these temporary measures be revoked because they were illegally and improperly entered; correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the next page, there's a paragraph that starts with "The accused Banjac Bosko." It says he file add motion on 6 January 2001, named answer to the charge, and stated in that objection that complainant's house -- that would be your house -- was devastated during the combat activities, as it was the case with other buildings that were the property of three nations in the whole Bosnia-Herzegovina. He denies taking part in any matter in the devastation of the complainant's house and requests from the complainant to revoke the complaint and from the Court to revoke the temporary measure forbidding the handling of his real estate. The third accused Rasula Nedjeljko filed an objection on 3 March 2000 named answer to the charge, saying it was untrue that he ordered the demolition of anyone's house, which applies for the complainant's house as well. He contests the legal foundation for the complaint and asked for revocation." And then at the end of that next paragraph with Grbic and Dusanka people -- the last couple of sentences it says: "In the end it is stated that there is no legal ground for holding the accused Saovic Slobodanka, Indjic Jelena, Cucum Danica, and Grbic Dusanka responsible for the complainant's damage. He proposed to the Court to revoke the temporary measures." Then the Court makes its decision: "In the opinion of this Court, there was no legal foundation for issuing temporary measures that forebode the alienation and burden of the real estate belonging to the accused from Article 266, paragraph 1.2 ZIP, namely in accordance with Article 265, paragraph 1 ZIP, temporary measure can be issued if the creditor, that is, complainant, shows as probable the existence of the claim and danger that without such a measure, the debtor -- that is, the accused could obstruct or significantly complicate the payment of the creditor's claim in this case, the complainant's. The Court could not determine from the complaint or the decision which particular actions could the accused undertake in order to complicate the payment of the complainant's claim. Besides, the Court did not have legal foundation for issuing decision for temporary measures in relation to Saovic Darinka who died in 1993, and as such could not be a party in the procedure, in which manner the Court determined that the accused Saovic Slobodanka, Indjic Jelena, Cucum Danica, and Grbic Dusanka are the legal beneficiaries of Saovic - born Lavic - Derinka [phoen], is not visible from the documents since there is no decision on inheritance. Finally it should be stated that the decision for temporary number measures, number P419/99, dated 22 November 1999 is in contrast to the annex 7 of the Dayton Agreement and especially with the agreement on refugees and displaced persons, Article 11, mandate, Article 12, procedure before the commission, point 2 and 6 where it is said, and we quote 'for every person who requests repatriation of the property and the commission establishes that he/she is the legal owner of that property, it will be repatriated. In every person who requests compensation and exchange of the repatriation and the commission establishes that he/she is the legal owner of that property, the just compensation will be given and it will be determined by the commission.' In point 6 it is said: "In the case when the creditor was granted with the compensation in exchange of repatriation of property, the commission can grant a financial indemnity or compensatory bond for future purchasing of real estate." And then finally, contrary to the order entered by Judge Edina, this Court says: "It is possible to appeal this decision." Now, Judge, from what we've looked at, it appears that you filed a case without legal foundation in your own court, as the judge in the court where you were the president of the court. That judge entered illegal orders and tied up property for 18 months. And only when it got to a court over which you apparently had no control did these temporary measures get revoked and was it pointed out that what you had asked the judge to do in Sanski Most was to enter an order that violated not just the law of Bosnia-Herzegovina but the Dayton Accords. My question is: Do judges in the lower courts of Bosnia-Herzegovina have any kind of ethical responsibilities?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Judge. The question may be a little bit long. Actually, the question is very simple. It's the last part, because the rest is a statement that Mr. Ackerman is making. And the question actually is: Do you judges in the lower courts of Bosnia-Herzegovina have any kind of ethical responsibility -- so code of ethics or ethical rules that you are bound to follow? If I have used words or phrases that do not reflect what you stated, Mr. Ackerman, please correct me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's fine, Judge.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course we do. Of course we do. By your leave, I would just like to say something very brief. This is a civil suit. What was decided by the municipal court is a decision or a temporary measure banning alienation. However, that does not mean that the judge worked without any feeling of conscience or a set of criteria. This is a case that is underway in Bosanska Krupa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can stop there. In other words, do I take it that you have appealed this decision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't submitted an appeal. The proceedings continue. This is an ongoing case. The temporary measure was stopped, and I did not complain about that. However, probably during these proceedings I have the intention of moving once again for imposing a new temporary measure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman in the course of this lengthy attack on the judge ended up by making a statement which in my view was in any event misleading on what he'd read out that this was an illegal and whatever procedure. That is not the case. And the judge is entitled to explain that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. He's perfectly entitled to explain that. And I'm not stopping him from explaining that. When I stopped him is stating that he has intentions maybe later on to bring up the question of reviving the injunction --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the judge is entitled to explain that he didn't appeal the temporary restraining order, that the action against these men is continued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I let him state that. And if there is anything else that he'd like to add, he is free to add it, but not what he intends to do in the future. Yes, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there anything else you would like to add before you are re-examined by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just briefly, by your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. But please be brief, because you have only 12 minutes left. And if we don't finish in those 12 minutes, it means you have to come again Monday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I had already made the decision that such re-examinations I had are not worth keeping the judge here for. And I think he's entitled to answer in the way he wishes what has just been put to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I will let him say what he wants. Yes, Judge, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wished to say that this complaint of mine is a matter of principle for compensation for the damages sustained, the damage I sustained as a citizen. All the property my wife and I acquired over the past 15 or 20 years of our work was ruthlessly and in a bloodthirsty manner destroyed and seized within 15 minutes' time. I lodged this complaint as a matter of principle. And as for this complaint of mine and as for the proceedings that are ongoing before the Court in Krupa, I shall go on with that against those persons from whom according to civil law I have the right to sue for compensation of damages. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to make sure that I understand this cross-examination. It is suggested that because of a civil suit, is it, the judge has invented his evidence about the destruction of Mahala?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's being suggested that he has an interest in convincing this Court that there was no resistance in Mahala and that therefore -- yeah. But anyway, let me let -- let me have Mr. Ackerman respond to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: In the face of this evidence to the contrary and throughout the testimony, even when not asked, this judge has gratuitously thrown in that there was no fighting in Mahala that, there was no fighting in Mahala, that there was no fighting in Mahala, that nobody was armed and nobody had weapons. And Your Honour, a finding by this Tribunal that there was no fighting in Mahala could be used by him, I think, in his lawsuit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I got your point. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's my point. And I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In other words, I did not misunderstand him at any given moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And the other point is that the Krupa Court ruled that the order entered by Judge Edina from his court was illegal and improper. That was the other point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But let's --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I'm sorry. I still don't -- I don't understand, I should say, because that's -- purpose of any re-examination. What is the purpose of this cross-examination? In other words, is it suggested that the judge has either erred in his factual description, is lying in his factual description, has forged documents -- because clearly there's an allegation impliedly being made that he didn't sign this document. Though what issue that goes to, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know either at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But Your Honour, I want to understand what it is -- and the witness ought to be given an opportunity. That is the point of 90(H).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The witness is -- first of all, he's a judge and he should understand. There is a very clear-cut allegation of dishonesty that is being thrown in his regard by Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And he's the one to -- I was going to say stand up and answer to that if he has an answer. But it's up to him. I'm not going to stop him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, no. I'm sorry. It's obviously my fault. I'm not making myself clear. I do not from what I have listened to, the cross-examination in -- I understand Madam Fauveau's cross-examination perfectly. It is an allegation that somehow he is involved with forgery of a map for example and the diary. I do not understand from Mr. Ackerman's cross-examination -- and I think we are entitled to understand, as is the witness -- what it is suggested that this witness has not done or done or whatever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I think --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. You are right. Let's go through it bit by bit or one by one in these six -- seven minutes. Mr. Ackerman, are you suggesting that the witness -- this is how I understood you. Are you suggesting that the witness lied to the Trial Chamber when he said that there was no resistance, no fighting in Mahala?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm suggesting that it's highly probable that he did because of the lawsuit that he has. It's worth 100.000 Deutschmarks to him. That's what I'm suggesting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In my mind, it's all tied up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I don't know that he lied. I wasn't there. But I'm suggesting that it's highly probable that he did. I'm also suggesting that it's highly probable that one of those signatures that we saw today is not his. Just looking at it, any one would conclude that one of those signatures can't be his, because it's written very different. It's a completely different handwriting. Now, whether I'm right about that or not, it's going to depend I suppose on a handwriting expert looking at it and giving us an opinion. And the Prosecutor will be free to have a handwriting expert look at it too. And so whether that turns out -- if my suspicion about that is correct or not, I don't know. But I'm not a handwriting expert, so I can't make that conclusion, and I don't know what Ms. Korner wants from me. But I'm -- I think I've made it clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's why I've said let's go through it bit by bit. And are you suggesting that there is a motive behind what you're suspecting, namely that if the witness convinces this Trial Chamber that there was no fighting in Mahala, then that would suit or improve his chances in the civil case that he has been testifying about?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If he could get this Court to make that finding -- this is perhaps the most prestigious Court in the world doing this kind of work right now. That authority would be more than persuasive --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's the interest. It's a 100.000 Deutschemark interest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And finally, are you suggesting that as regards the proceedings in Sanski Most or wherever -- where Edina -- Judge Edina was presiding, he manipulated the situation? Are you making that suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I have no basis upon which to make that, but it's -- I think it's highly probable. I don't think there's a country in the world where the president of the court can file a lawsuit in his own court and have one of his own judges decide his own case. Somebody figured out after that order was entered that what was going on there was improper and it needed to be sent away. It should have been sent away -- he should have known to send it away to another court immediately. He was the president of the court. He should have known that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And are you making any other allegation -- Or Ms. Korner, are you thinking of any other allegation --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. Your Honour, this is actually -- I'm sorry. This is the most incredible, if I may say so, conversation that Mr. Ackerman -- or speech that Mr. Ackerman is making. It is improper to make these sort of suggestions that he has been making without the slightest foundation for so doing so. What is more -- Your Honour, my question was a simple straightforward one. This witness has given clear and unambiguous evidence of the events that he says took place in Sanski Most, of the events that he says happened to him in Manjaca, of the documents that were found in Sanski Most which he has produced. My simple question is: Is any of that evidence as to fact that he has given challenged? Is it to be suggested that he has manufactured in some way or was a party to the manufacture of the documents which we have produced in the bundle? That's all that I want to know before this witness leaves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm a defence lawyer. It's the Prosecutor's job to prove this case beyond a reasonable doubt. I am challenging that proof every way that I know how. I think there is ample basis for suggesting that this witness was not being truthful about what happened in Sanski Most. Much of what he said about what happened in Sanski Most happened while he was in a cell that he couldn't even see out of. So he can't possibly know about some of the things that he has told you are facts, like destruction of his house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As I see it, Ms. Korner, you are perfectly right. I can actually understand very well the problem that you're --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm not going to -- I'm not going to pursue this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the thing -- I think the allegation is very -- is a very straightforward one. Mr. Ackerman has tried all along to discredit this witness, presenting him as a dishonest person. This is how I take it. Am I right, Mr. Ackerman? It doesn't mean to say that he has not told us the truth in everything. I mean, but this is how Mr. Ackerman, I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You're absolutely right. And from yesterday, when I accused him of stealing a roof until today, when I accused him of forgery and improper judicial behaviour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And this is --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think there's evidence supporting all of those.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He didn't actually accuse the judge of forgery. He accused someone else unknown of forging the judge's signature, which makes it even curiouser.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: She's absolutely right. I did. But he said it was his signature. So I was accusing him of not speaking the truth about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Judge, I hope that the proceedings in your court are less troublesome than they are here. I take this opportunity to thank you for coming here, for giving evidence. You don't need the witness for any re-examination, I understand it, Ms. Korner. No?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, after what has just transpired, I would think it an insult to the witness to re-examine him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I object pretty strongly to that. It would not be an insult to the witness to re-examine him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And that's just an outrageous remark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, please. Not in front of the witness, in any case. Once more, I thank you for coming here on my behalf and on behalf of the other two Judges, and I wish you a safe journey home. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only thing that I'm going to draw your attention to -- and I don't need the witness to do it, because Mr. Ackerman declined -- but if Your Honour does -- and Your Honours -- I'm sorry. Go to the P227 for your own time in the 18th of May, you will find there the decision which refers to item number 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You've side it -- you've said it already. Actually.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I think the witness can be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Allow me to thank the Honourable Trial Chamber, the Office of the Prosecution and all the court officers. I am deeply offended as a person and as a professional, deeply. That's what I wish to say. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Monday we start with the new witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the session -- the court is adjourned until Monday at -- we'll still be -- 9.00 in the morning, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: at 1.46 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 27th day of May, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
